sn.c: The Mezzanine overhang begins over Orchestra row H, and from row N back it cuts off the top of the stage.
sn.sh: Overhang cuts off the top of the stage from row N

sn.c: The six-seat Boxes beside the Orchestra are elevated and close, but the view is angled toward the stage.
The Mezzanine has the cheapest seats in the house at the back and far sides, and its steep rake and the small room keep views strong.
sn.sh: Cheapest seats in the house with a steep, clear rake

sn.c: Orchestra legroom is much better than at a typical Broadway house, and aisle seats have the most room.
Mezzanine legroom is usually better than average for Broadway.

vs.sum: Completed a major renovation in early 2026 with all seats replaced and legroom expanded, making it one of Broadway's most comfortable and modern houses. New restrooms significantly reduce intermission wait times.

acc.note: Elevators to all levels. 53 assistive listening devices. 11 wheelchair seats across Orchestra and Balcony.
